'''Andrea Rica Nahmod''' (born 1964)<ref>Birth year from [http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2012050375.html Library of Congress catalog entry], retrieved 2019-01-19.</ref> is an American mathematician at [[University of Massachusetts, Amherst]].<ref name=home>{{cite web|url=http://people.math.umass.edu/~nahmod/|place=University of Massachusetts, Amherst Math Department|title=Andrea R. Nahmod|accessdate=Feb 27, 2015}}</ref> She is known for her work in [[nonlinear partial differential equation]]s nonlinear Fourier analysis, and [[harmonic analysis]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Three Faculty Members Receive Lifetime Honorific of Provost Professor : UMass Amherst |url=https://www.umass.edu/news/article/three-faculty-members-receive-lifetime-honorific-provost-professor |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=www.umass.edu |language=en}}</ref>

==Eearly Life and Education==
Nahmod was born in [[Buenos Aires|Buenos Aires, Argentina]],<ref name=":0" /> into a family of physicians and medical researchers.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Spotlight Scholars Archive : UMass Amherst |url=https://www.umass.edu/gateway/spotlight-scholars-archive |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=www.umass.edu |language=en}}</ref>

During her childhood and early university years in Argentina, which coincided with the military dictatorship (1976–1983), she found mathematics to be a source of intellectual stability amid political turmoil. Although she initially intended to study medicine, her interest in the mathematical foundations of genetics and the encouragement of a former neighbor working in astrophysics led her to pursue a career in mathematics.<ref name=":1" />

She earned a Licenciatura en Matemática (equivalent to an M.Sc. in Mathematics) from the Faculty of Exact and Natural Sciences at the [[University of Buenos Aires]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Lathisms |url=https://www.lathisms.org/calendar-2023/dr-andrea-r-nahmod |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=www.lathisms.org}}</ref> Her Thesis advisor was [[Cora Sadosky]] who also helped her pursue her Ph.D in the US.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Margaret A. Readdy and Christine Taylor |date=March 2018 |title=Women’s History Month |url=https://www.ams.org/publications/notices/rnoti-p248.pdf |journal=Notices of the AMS |volume=65 |issue=3 |pages=282-283}}</ref>

Nahmod received her Ph.D. from [[Yale University]] in 1991 under the supervision of [[Ronald Coifman|Ronald R. Coifman]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=39118|title=Andrea Rica Nahmod}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> She went to work as a research fellow at Macquarie University from 1992 to 1994, followed by positions at [[University of Texas, Austin]], the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]], and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], before coming to work at [[University of Massachusetts, Amherst]] in 1998.<ref name="home" /><ref>{{cite conference |url=http://www.math.unm.edu/conferences/10thAnalysis/lecturers.html |title=Main Lecturers |date=October 11–12, 2007 |publisher=University of New Mexico |conference=Tenth New Mexico Analysis Seminar}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
She has organized research programs at institutions including the [[Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute|Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] (MSRI) at the [[University of California]], Berkeley, and the [[Institute for Computational and Experimental Research in Mathematics]] (ICERM) at [[Brown University]].<ref name=":2" />

==Awards and honors==
In 2013, Nahmod became a [[Simons Foundation|Simons Fellow]].<ref name=Simon>{{cite web|url=http://www.umass.edu/newsoffice/article/nahmod-named-simons-fellow-2013-14|place=UMass Amherst News and Media Relations|title=Nahmod named Simons Fellow for 2013-14|accessdate=Feb 27, 2015}}</ref>

In 2014, Nahmod became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref> The society cited her “contributions to nonlinear Fourier analysis, harmonic analysis, and partial differential equations, as well as service to the mathematical community.”<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.umass.edu/newsoffice/article/nahmod-named-fellow-american-mathematical|place=UMass Amherst News and Media Relations|title=Nahmod Named a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society|accessdate=Feb 27, 2015}}</ref>

Nahmod was named [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] Simons Professor for 2015-2016.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-06-07|website=www.msri.org}}</ref>

She was also awarded the Sargent-Faul Fellowship at the [[Harvard Radcliffe Institute|Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study]] and the Chern Professorship.<ref name=":2" />

==Selected publications==
* Nahmod, Andrea; Stefanov, Atanas; [[Karen Uhlenbeck|Uhlenbeck, Karen]]. On Schrödinger maps. ''Comm. Pure Appl. Math.'' 56 (2003), no. 1, 114–151.
* Auscher, Pascal; McIntosh, Alan; Nahmod, Andrea. Holomorphic functional calculi of operators, quadratic estimates and interpolation. ''Indiana Univ. Math. J.'' 46 (1997), no. 2, 375–403.
* Gilbert, John E.; Nahmod, Andrea R. Bilinear operators with non-smooth symbol. ''I. J. Fourier Anal. Appl.'' 7 (2001), no. 5, 435–467.
* Nahmod, Andrea; Stefanov, Atanas; Uhlenbeck, Karen. On the well-posedness of the wave map problem in high dimensions. ''Comm. Anal. Geom.'' 11 (2003), no. 1, 49–83.
